x: Les Stokell ran his usual determined kind of race while Jack Brown seemed content to take matters easy in front of Archie Bedford, Steve Charlton and Jack Bragginton.
On his leg he actually led the S.L.H. runner by about 200 yards and this lead was never lost, and Jack Bragginton on the second stage increased our advantage to 52 secs.
In the 3 miles Team Race we had Jack Bragginton, George Lucas, Steve Charlton and Len Bishop, but could only manage a 4th place in this event.

Gordon Lowers retained his 100 yards title in the good time of 10.6 secs, on a very heavy track, and then Ches Walker won the 1 mile in 4 mins. 28.8 secs. with Bob Taylor in second place. Jack Bragginton was third in the 3 miles run which was won in a new record time, while in the Junior events we had D.
Ches Walker went off first for us and he beat Stone of Dorking and Martin of Walton A.C. to give Jack Bragginton a useful lead, and his time of 14 mins. 12 secs. beat the previous course record.
Jack Brown, however, had other ideas and with a lap to go he went well ahead to win in 15 min. 19.2 secs., with Jack Bragginton just beating Archie Bedford for second place.

Arthur Bruce was our next runner and although he did second fastest time the Reading man increased his side's lead. Jack Bragginton then went off and ran well to gain half-a-minute on the leader but our last runner, Ches Walker, had J.

Although Jack Bragginton was our first man home in seventh position, Archie Bedford inspired the team by his forward running in the early stages, and the others were always striving to overtake him, which eventually Bragginton and Bob Taylor managed to do.

The first lap was slow, with the field well bunched, as our lads did not know the course, but during the latter stages John Bromley, Jack Brown and Bill Lucas took command, although Wells, of the home club, did his best to hang on, closely followed by Jack Bragginton and Ray Tooby.

In both events Belgrave were well to the fore, as in the senior event Ted Stimpson, Bill Lucas, Archie Bedford, Vern Blowfield, Eric Herbert, Jack Bragginton and Steve Charlton were well up, and Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor were in the lead in the junior race.

Jack Bragginton just managed to beat Bill Lucas by the proverbial “hairbreadth” on the finishing line, and they were closely followed by Archie Bedford and Jimmy Wood, and the latter must think it strange to finish 15th and not score in the winning team.

Jack Bragginton ran his usual dogged race and Len Adams maintained his recent improvement by finishing on Jack's heels. Eddie Short was our sixth scoring man in 29th position, and seeing that he is now serving in the R.A.F., Eddie can be said to have done very well.
